source.test: createBackup(...) success branch has no structural verification before visibility

phase6_correction.reuses: the same archive-safety structural check P6.5 built for fixtures/world-archive-safety (rejects traversal, absolute paths, symlinks, corrupt central-directory entries)
phase6_correction.unverified_or_failed_archives: still reported (never hidden) but excluded from the restorable set until re-verified

notes: D-006-style correction, not oracle parity. MSC 1 treats a zero zip exit status as sufficient (lines 276-292): it writes the sidecar and reloads the list with no read-back or structural check of the archive it just wrote. restoreBackup's own validateZipArchive call (line 656) only runs later, at restore time, per-attempt -- never at creation/listing time. Phase 6 moves that check earlier so a corrupt-on-write backup (e.g. disk full mid-zip, /usr/bin/zip silently truncated) is flagged when it's created, not discovered mid-restore days later.
